He's partially correct that their encrypted traffic was still safe. However if they're malicious and using something like a WiFi Pineapple they can break SSL and still see it. Never a good idea to send sensitive credentials or information over an unknown/untrusted WiFi hotspot.

On a side note, the WiFi Pineapple can also connect to a device that has wifi on and is trying to connect to a SSID that is, say, their home network. The device says "Hey, is Linksys available" WiFi Pineapple can be configured to see it calling out and says "I sure I'll be your huckleberry" and then your device is connected to what it thinks is a trusted WiFi network.

EDIT: Granted this was posted in 2010, and I don't know if technology like the WiFi Pineapple existed around that time.

Hey, thanks for the shoutout @mick ;p. I actually just auditioned for the voice and didn't make it this time unfortunately. I haven't recorded myself in a while but this is a song I recorded a few years ago. Pretty much everything on that channel is pretty rough but hey, it's what I got ;p.

I am no expert but you definitely have some things you could work on (we all do). You definitely have potential, you have a nice voice and can keep a pitch so you are already way ahead of most people. The main thing I would say to work on is breath support and making your sound fuller. When you sing your vocal chords come together and one way to sing which is appropriate sometimes is having an airy feel to it where you let some air through. You seem to more or less do this all the time which isn't bad but you should learn how to belt and how to have a full sound as well.

One more thing I would say is to work on consistently staying right on a pitch. I'm not saying you are out of tune because for the most part you aren't but you tend to swoop up and down to get to the notes, which again can be an effective style but I think you need to cut back on it a little bit.

Mainly just keep on singing and be honest with yourself. I am my own harshest critic and while that is sometimes not great, it can be useful, always try to find things you can improve on.

As for auditioning, you can do it for the experience if you like but I can tell you there is pretty much a 0% chance you will make it with your current ability. I'm not trying to be mean but it's just how it is, especially for the Voice. When I went professional musicians and people who were better than me in a lot of ways got turned away. It's just as much about being a sell-able and likable brand then it is your voice because a lot of people can sing well that audition but only a very very small minority get through.

Never give up though if it is your passion. It is not an easy thing to excel in because the entirety of performing is filled with judgement and feeling you are not good enough but if you try hard enough anything is possible.
